scanUpdates.text: The summary names MASTER_W2_v24 and MASTER_CONSULTING_v22 as the current resume masters. Box also holds MASTER_W2_v25 (dated 2026-07-20) and MASTER_CONSULTING_v23 (dated 2026-07-20). Both are newer than the versions the summary names. Please confirm which pair is current.

A 29 Sep working note records that the July plan placed the firm under Impact Arts Society LLC (Delaware), trading as "Olmsted Data Advisory Group". The 29 Sep confirmation says "Olmsted Data Advisory", without "Group". The same note finds no record assigning either name to a legal entity or a Washington filing.
rbolmsted.com is on record as registered 2026-09-23 through Cloudflare on a five-year term. This matches the summary.
The scan did not read the records that could answer the original 18 questions and 4 job-search items. They are all treated as open. The 14 new questions are open too.

14 questions were added from two supplied sources: the Super Interviews LinkedIn audit workshop recording (8 Oct 2025) and the Salesforce 50 Best Practices for Email Marketers guide. Advice is labeled by source. Prices, offers, success claims and statistics from both sources are not used.
The workshop advises naming well-known employers in a headline. That conflicts with the round-one exclusion in version 1.1, so the headline question says not to.

sections.title: Facts only you can supply
sections.blurb: Figures and dates from your own records. The strategy holds labeled placeholders in their place, and nothing was invented.

questions.title: Current audience and pipeline counts
questions.prompt: What are your current LinkedIn followers, email contacts, newsletter subscribers and pipeline counts?
questions.why: Real numbers replace the labeled starting-state scenarios in the funnel math.
questions.advice: For email contacts, count only people whose source you know and who agreed to hear from you. Quality counts for more than the size of the list.

questions.title: Recent contract and consulting rates
questions.prompt: What have your recent contract and consulting rates been?
questions.why: The revenue scenarios need a real rate range.

questions.title: Weekly hours after a job
questions.prompt: Do your 15 to 20 weekly hours continue after you take a job?
questions.why: The employment-transition scenario cannot resolve without this answer.

questions.title: LinkedIn newsletter status
questions.prompt: What is your LinkedIn newsletter eligibility, Creator Mode status and subscriber notification setting?
questions.why: It decides whether a LinkedIn newsletter is available alongside the main newsletter.

questions.title: Engagement-count convention
questions.prompt: Which engagement-count convention do you want to use in public?
questions.why: Public claims need one counting rule that stays the same across posts.
questions.advice: Open rates are becoming unreliable. The guide suggests click-through rate, subscriber growth and unsubscribes as firmer measures. Pick one counting rule and keep it the same in public.

questions.title: The Lam validation protocol
questions.prompt: Did you design the Lam validation protocol, or teach and refine an existing one?
questions.why: The answer shapes the wording, although this claim sits behind the round-one exclusion either way.

questions.title: DAMA CDMP exam scores and dates
questions.prompt: What was your exact score on each DAMA CDMP exam, and on what date?
questions.why: The register holds no verified scores or dates yet.

questions.title: BackOffice no-code classes
questions.prompt: What were the dates and course names for your BackOffice no-code classes?
questions.why: No pass-rate claim will appear until a record supports it.

sections.title: Permissions and clearances
sections.blurb: Two of these need an outside reviewer. Reading an agreement yourself does not equal advice on it.

questions.title: Accenture and Lam agreement limits
questions.prompt: Do your Accenture or Lam agreements restrict publicity, client references, non-solicitation, or use of engagement figures?
questions.why: The whole round-one exclusion guards against this risk.

questions.title: Employer outside-activity policy
questions.prompt: Does any prospective employer's written outside-activity policy permit consulting, a paid newsletter and public commentary?
questions.why: Employment is an equal fourth objective. If a policy forbids the other three, the plan changes shape.

questions.title: Names of organizations and quote permission
questions.prompt: Confirm the correct names of the organizations recalled, and say whether anyone will give written permission to be quoted.
questions.why: Recalled so far: Lam, Dow, Purdue, Chevron, and one name lost to a transcription error. None are quoted or treated as testimonials.

questions.title: Scope of the round-one exclusion
questions.prompt: Does the round-one exclusion also cover private consulting conversations and job interviews?
questions.why: The working assumption is no, meaning published content only. Sales and interview scripts depend on your answer.

questions.title: Agency case-study permission
questions.prompt: Will you give Miah written permission to present the operating system and selected assets as an agency case study?
questions.why: This permission is separate from the work itself and has not been granted.

sections.title: Decide together with Miah
sections.blurb: Add your view here. Miah reads it before the two of you settle each item.

questions.title: Firm name
questions.prompt: Which firm name do you want? On 13 September you said you did not want the family surname in the firm name and left naming to Miah. On 29 September she confirmed "Olmsted Data Advisory".
questions.why: The two records conflict, so please agree on one. The 29 September working note also lists the July plan name as "Olmsted Data Advisory Group", under Impact Arts Society LLC.

questions.title: Newsletter brand name
questions.prompt: Which newsletter brand name do you choose? "The Sign-Off" is a proposal, not a decision. The name, domain and handles still need an availability check.
questions.why: Nothing is published or purchased under the name until you decide.

questions.title: What covers Miah's pay in months 1 to 3
questions.prompt: What covers Miah's pay in months 1 to 3, before business revenue can?
questions.why: Her requirement is $4,000 to $6,000 a month. The six-month target is $5,000 to $10,000 combined gross, including your employment income. Internal transfers are not double-counted.

questions.title: Is the monthly figure before or after tax?
questions.prompt: Is the $4,000 to $6,000 figure before or after tax?
questions.why: It has no owner yet, and it changes the revenue math.

questions.title: When round two begins
questions.prompt: When does round two begin, and what would justify seeking clearance to reference recent engagements?
questions.why: It has no owner yet.

sections.title: Your job-search files
sections.blurb: Open since July. Record what you did, or what is blocking you.

questions.title: Client Experience Application
questions.prompt: Fill in the Client Experience Application before Miah's review gate. It overlaps the Engagement History One-Pager, which awaits approval, so the two need reconciling.
questions.why: Miah's review gate waits on it.

questions.title: Lyra Health VP resume variant
questions.prompt: Verify the Lyra Health VP standalone resume variant. What did you find?
questions.why: Open since July.

questions.title: Fujitsu portal resume
questions.prompt: Which resume did the Fujitsu portal actually receive?
questions.why: Open since July.

questions.title: Resume masters in use
questions.prompt: Which resume masters are current? The summary says nine custom resumes and the cover letters use version 21, and names MASTER_W2_v24 and MASTER_CONSULTING_v22 as the masters. A 1 Oct scan of Box also found MASTER_W2_v25 and MASTER_CONSULTING_v23. Miah decides on a refresh, but it affects anything you send next.
questions.why: It affects anything you send next.
questions.advice: The workshop says to tailor the resume to each role and to keep LinkedIn broader than any one resume. That supports refreshing the masters before the next send.

sections.title: Your LinkedIn profile
sections.blurb: New. Questions drawn from the LinkedIn audit workshop. The advice is opinion from a vendor, so each item says where it comes from.

questions.title: Target role for your LinkedIn profile
questions.prompt: What one role or kind of engagement should your LinkedIn profile attract first? For example, advisory work for business leaders, or a director-level data strategy role.
questions.why: Employment is an equal fourth objective next to consulting, the newsletter and public commentary. One profile has to serve all four.
questions.advice: A good headline names the role you are going for and what makes you unique. Keep LinkedIn broad enough to fit a few role types, but not so narrow that it only suits one company. The résumé is where you go narrow.

questions.title: Headline draft
questions.prompt: Write a draft headline of up to about 220 characters. Say who you help, in what role, and your edge.
questions.why: The headline is the part recruiters and prospects see in search results.
questions.advice: Lead with your current role and scope. Use one or at most two metrics. State what makes you different, tightly enough to scan like an ad headline.
questions.caution: The workshop also suggests naming well-known companies. Version 1.1 excludes every Lam Research and Accenture reference, including by date, sector or role. Do not use those names, and do not claim a dollar figure for what your approach saved anyone.

questions.title: Opening impact for your About section
questions.prompt: What is the single most impressive piece of impact in your career that you are free to describe in public? Say how you did it. Mark each fact as verified, recalled or an estimate.
questions.why: The About section opens with your strongest evidence. The register keeps verified evidence, recollections and modeled scenarios separate.
questions.advice: The About section does three jobs: show your most impressive impact fast, summarize your other experience briefly, and end with a call to action.
questions.caution: It must sit outside the round-one exclusion. If the best example comes from Lam or Accenture work, say so here and Miah will route it to the "Then and Now" series instead.

questions.title: Call to action for the About section
questions.prompt: Who should contact you from your About section, and what should they do? For example, business leaders weighing a data decision can message you to talk it through.
questions.why: A reader who stays 30 seconds is a peer, a recruiter or a prospect. Give each one a next step.
questions.advice: End the About section with a direct invitation aimed at the people you want to hear from.

questions.title: Roles to detail first in Experience
questions.prompt: Which three roles should be rewritten first? For each, give the scope, team size and one or two outcomes you can stand behind. Mark each fact as verified, recalled or an estimate.
questions.why: No numbers are filled in for you. Miah will draft only from facts you supply.
questions.advice: Write Experience first, then About, then the headline. Describe scope, outcomes and team size. If you were promoted, show the change in scope.

questions.title: Has your profile changed since July?
questions.prompt: The Box folder holds "Bob Olmsted LinkedIn Profile July 2026.pdf". Has your profile changed since then? If it has, please save a fresh copy to PDF and send it to Miah.
questions.why: Any rewrite starts from the current profile.
questions.advice: The workshop says LinkedIn can save a profile as a PDF, and that the PDF is a good input for reviewing the profile.
questions.sourceRef: Workshop 0:29. The save-to-PDF step is the vendor's description; check it in LinkedIn.

sections.title: Interviews and conversations
sections.blurb: New. Drawn from the same workshop.

questions.title: The wins you return to
questions.prompt: Which two or three career wins do you want to tell in every interview and sales conversation? One sentence each. Mark each as verified, recalled or an estimate.
questions.why: Q-23 asks whether private conversations fall under the exclusion. Your answer there decides which wins you can use in sales and interview scripts.
questions.advice: Lead with your wins. Spend little time on career breaks or mistakes, and tie each win to the problem the other person has.

questions.title: Opening answer and a spoken practice
questions.prompt: In a few sentences, why are you doing this work? That is the start of your "tell me about yourself" answer. Then, will you do a spoken run-through with Miah before your next interview or discovery call? Give a date if you can.
questions.why: Employment is one of the four objectives, so interviews matter.
questions.advice: Open with your reason, not a list of jobs. Keep the structure clear, practice out loud rather than only in writing, and leave room for the other person to talk.

sections.title: The newsletter
sections.blurb: New. Drawn from a vendor email guide.

questions.title: Who the newsletter is for and what they get
questions.prompt: In one sentence, who reads the newsletter and what do they get from each issue? The working name is "The Sign-Off", and Q-08 settles the name.
questions.why: The Shared Operating Strategy compares Substack and beehiiv. A one-sentence purpose helps decide between them.
questions.advice: Write a short statement you can give anyone who asks what you are working on. Set goals around what the reader gains, and focus less on the sell.

questions.title: How often you can publish
questions.prompt: How often can you publish for the next six months and keep it up? Think about your 15 to 20 weekly hours and Q-05.
questions.why: Revenue scenarios assume a steady publishing rhythm.
questions.advice: Consistent volume and frequency matter more than occasional bursts. Start with a pace you can hold.

questions.title: Where your email contacts came from
questions.prompt: Where did your email contacts come from, and which of them have agreed to get a newsletter from you? If you are not sure, say so.
questions.why: Q-01 asks for the contact count. This tells Miah how many can be invited and how.
questions.advice: Ask for permission clearly, tell people what they will get and how often, and make unsubscribing one click. Do not email an address if you do not know where it came from.
questions.caution: Rules on bulk email depend on where you and your readers live. Ask a qualified advisor if you are unsure. This page is not legal advice.

questions.title: How you will measure the newsletter
questions.prompt: Which measures matter to you most? For example, subscriber growth, clicks, replies, unsubscribes or new conversations.
questions.why: It feeds Q-10, the engagement-count convention for public use.
questions.advice: Set the measures before you send. Prefer click-through, deliverability and bounce rate over open rates, and tie results to business outcomes.

questions.title: Sending address and platform setup
questions.prompt: Should the newsletter send from your own domain, such as rbolmsted.com, or from the platform's domain? Who will handle the domain settings?
questions.why: A custom sending domain needs setup so mail is trusted. This overlaps with Miah's Cloudflare work.
questions.advice: Set up email authentication (SPF and DKIM) so your mail is verified as yours. Start with small sends to your best contacts, then build up volume.

questions.title: First issue
questions.prompt: What is the one message of the first issue? Add a draft subject line of about 50 characters or fewer, and a one-line preview of about 100 characters.
questions.why: Nothing is sent. This only drafts the first issue for your review.
questions.advice: One message per email. Trim the copy, make the action clear, test how it looks on a phone and with images off, and run a small test before a full send.
